sections.h2: How do you sell a house in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin, without a long wait?
sections.html:
A Mount Pleasant owner can list with an agent, sell privately, or take a cash offer from a buyer who purchases the house as it is. Cash works best when repairs, a probate delay or a move date make showings and buyer financing hard to manage.

The Census Bureau puts Mount Pleasant's July 1, 2025 population at 28,253, up 1.8 percent from the 2020 estimates base. About 76.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied home was valued at $292,400 for 2020 to 2024. Median household income was $91,616, and the average household has 2.33 people.

sections.h2: Where is Mount Pleasant and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Mount Pleasant is a village in Racine County, about 30 miles south of Milwaukee and 60 miles north of Chicago. Settlement began in 1835, residents organized the Town of Mount Pleasant in 1842, and the community incorporated as a village on September 16, 2003, after a referendum. The village adopted its zoning ordinance in 1972, so land-use rules have been set locally for decades. Its land area is about 34 square miles, which gives it roughly 818 people per square mile.

A six-member board of trustees and an elected village president govern the village, and it has its own police department. The village runs its own sanitary sewer and storm water utilities, buys drinking water from the city of Racine, and has building, planning, engineering and finance departments in house. Fire and ambulance service comes from the South Shore Fire Department.

The Census Bureau counted 11,883 households for 2020 to 2024, with 2.33 people per household. Roughly one in five residents is under 18, and 22 percent are 65 or older, so buyers include retirees as well as families.

sections.h2: What do the big development projects mean for a Mount Pleasant seller?
sections.html:
Large projects have shaped the village's recent story. Foxconn announced a $10 billion display campus in October 2017 as part of the Wisconn Valley Science and Technology Park, and the plan was later scaled back. In September 2025 Microsoft announced construction of a large data center in Mount Pleasant.

Buyers sometimes ask what will be built near a house, so be ready for the question. Rather than guessing, direct them to the village's planning and engineering departments, which handle zoning and approvals for additions and new structures.

sections.h2: Which schools serve Mount Pleasant homes?
sections.html:
The Racine Unified School District runs the village's public schools. Elementary schools named for sections of the village include Dr. Jones, West Ridge, Schulte and the Gifford K-8 school, while Mitchell and Gifford K-8 schools serve middle school grades. Case High School is inside the village and serves almost all of it, and a few parts are zoned to Park High School in Racine.

Higher education sits close by. The University of Wisconsin-Parkside is about two miles south in Kenosha, and Gateway Technical College is nearby. A listing that names the exact school zone saves a buyer a phone call.

sections.h2: What permits and repairs should you sort out before selling in Mount Pleasant?
sections.html:
The village Building Inspection page says permits are taken through an online BS&A account, which is free to create. Its FAQ covers the rules that matter before a sale:

  • A building permit is required for new structures and for remodeling and alterations that qualify, and additions also need zoning and engineering approval.
  • One- and two-family projects follow the Uniform Dwelling Code, and electrical work follows the National Electric Code and SPS 316.
  • Homeowners may pull their own permits after reading and signing a Cautionary Statement, while contractors need the state dwelling contractor credentials.
  • Renovation work on housing built before 1978 must follow the state Lead Safe Rules.

Inspectors take calls from 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, and questions go to buildinginspection@mtpleasantwi.gov. If a past owner finished a deck, finished basement or garage without a permit, ask the department how to close the file before a buyer's inspector finds it.

sections.h2: Which Wisconsin sale rules apply in Mount Pleasant?
sections.html:
State law requires most sellers of one-to-four unit homes to deliver a condition report within 10 days after contract acceptance (Wis. Stat. 709.02). A buyer who gets nothing in that time has two business days after the window to cancel and recover deposits. A court-supervised fiduciary who never lived in the house is excused, which helps estate sellers.

The seller also pays the transfer fee, set at 30 cents per $100 of value by Wis. Stat. 77.22. A $300,000 price produces a $900 fee. Transfers by will, transfers between a parent and child for nominal consideration, and a deed to a mortgage holder under foreclosure are among the exemptions in section 77.25, and an exempt transfer still needs the reason stated on the deed.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded for a Mount Pleasant property?
sections.html:
Mount Pleasant is in Racine County, so deeds go to the Racine County Register of Deeds. The flat recording fee is $30, and the Wisconsin transfer fee is separate and is figured on the electronic transfer return. A termination of decedent's property interest (form HT-110) also costs $30.

The county's checklist says every document needs these items:

  • The grantor and grantee named.
  • A notarized or authenticated grantor signature.
  • A complete legal description and the parcel identification number.
  • The name of the person who drafted the document and a return address.
  • Legible text that follows the state margin and layout rules.

The office cannot help beyond basic information, so a title company or attorney normally prepares the deed.

sections.h2: When are Mount Pleasant property taxes due, and who gets the bill at closing?
sections.html:
Wisconsin assesses property at market value as of January 1, and the Department of Revenue's Guide for Property Owners says tax bills must be mailed by the third Monday in December. Installment payers owe the first half by January 31 and the second by July 31. Missing the first installment makes the entire balance delinquent as of February 1, with interest of 1 percent per month.

For the exact amount on a Mount Pleasant parcel, ask the village treasurer or the Racine County treasurer for a current statement. Your closing agent then splits the year's tax between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense in Mount Pleasant?
sections.html:
Listing gives access to buyers who use mortgages, but it brings showings, inspection requests and a financing timeline. A cash buyer pays without a lender and purchases as-is, so closing depends mainly on title work and your preferred date.

  • Ask for the offer in writing with the closing date and who pays title and recording costs.
  • Compare the net figure after your mortgage payoff and any liens, not the headline price.
  • Keep a copy of any permit records and the condition report so the buyer sees the same facts you do.
  • Gather the parcel number from your tax bill, your mortgage lender's name and any HOA or special assessment notices before the first call.

If the house sits in a probate matter, tell the buyer early who has authority to sign, because the deed must carry the right signatures and a notary's acknowledgment before the Racine County office will record it.

faqs.q: How many people live in Mount Pleasant?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimated 28,253 residents on July 1, 2025. The 2020 census count was 27,732.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Mount Pleasant?
faqs.a: The Racine Unified School District runs the village's public schools. Case High School serves almost all of the village, and a few areas are zoned to Park High School in Racine.

faqs.q: Can I pull my own building permit in Mount Pleasant?
faqs.a: Yes, a homeowner can, after reading and signing the Cautionary Statement on the village's forms page. Contractors on one- and two-family homes need state dwelling contractor credentials.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Racine County?
faqs.a: The recording fee is a flat $30. The Wisconsin transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value is added when it applies, and the seller owes it.

faqs.q: Do estate sellers need a condition report in Wisconsin?
faqs.a: Not if the personal representative or other court-supervised fiduciary never occupied the property, according to Wis. Stat. 709.01. A seller who lived in the house must still complete the report.
